title: Probe async-hook chat delivery to busy agents
body:
Probe whether chat can reach a BUSY agent through async hooks, with no added per-turn latency. Today posts to a Working agent are held until its turn ends (src/chat.rs tick_at), so an orchestrator sitting in `kanban wait` gets stale posts minutes late, one turn per post.

Constraint from the user: no sync hooks. Anything that delays every turn is rejected.

Verified in source/docs (needs end-to-end proof):
- Codex 0.163.0: async command hooks can return hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext. core/src/hook_runtime.rs drain_async_hook_results injects it into a running turn as a developer message (inject_hook_context_if_running) or at the next turn start. There is no asyncRewake, so an idle Codex cannot be woken by a hook. Keyboard delivery stays for idle agents.
- Claude Code: async additionalContext arrives on the next turn; asyncRewake + exit 2 wakes an idle Claude.
- Codex re-prompts hook trust when a hook's command/config changes (hooks/src/engine/discovery.rs hook_hash -> Modified). Changing the managed hook (src/agent_hooks.rs) costs users a /hooks re-trust.

Probe: an async PostToolUse hook that fetches pending posts for FOREMAN_TERMINAL_ID and returns them as additionalContext. Verify against installed Codex and Claude: delivery mid-turn, the latency added (should be none), and how the cursor/ack should advance so a post is never delivered by both hook and keyboard.

Deliverable: probe results + a design note (docs/chat-delivery.md section or spec in docs/superpowers/specs/). Do not ship the delivery change from this card. It changes the control plane and goes through foreman-change-control.
